record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of fuzzy metric spaces
record.context_brief: Completion of the fuzzy Gromov-Hausdorff space CFM.
record.original_question: With CFM denoting the fuzzy metric space of isometry classes of compact fuzzy metric spaces endowed with the fuzzy Gromov-Hausdorff metric, is CFM completable, and can the elements of such a completion be described naturally as complete separable fuzzy metric spaces?

evidence.quote: One can also conjecture that the fuzzy metric space CFM is completable (note that there are noncompletable fuzzy metric spaces [3]) and the elements of its completion can be naturally described as complete separable fuzzy metric spaces.

artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (e.g., 2025 results establishing a Gromov–Hausdorff compactness theorem for non-Archimedean fuzzy metric spaces) extends Gromov–Hausdorff theory to fuzzy settings, but no source found explicitly resolves whether CFM with the fuzzy Gromov–Hausdorff metric is completable with completion identifiable as complete separable fuzzy metric spaces. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Gromov-Hausdorff compactness theorem for non-Archimedean Fuzzy Metric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: A Gromov-Hausdorff fuzzy metric was introduced in the setting of compact non-Archimedean fuzzy metric spaces, allowing a fuzzy version of Gromov's completeness theorem.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work develops fuzzy Gromov–Hausdorff theory but does not settle completability of CFM in the general (non non-Archimedean) case.

status_evidence.title: On Principal Fuzzy Metric Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Fuzzy metric spaces, in general, are not completable; strongly principal fuzzy metric spaces with strong M with respect to an integral positive t-norm admit completion.
status_evidence.claim: Completability of fuzzy metric spaces is nontrivial; not all fuzzy metric spaces are completable, so the question for CFM is substantive.
